piece: W1-19 — the main quest, end to end
corpus_item: RI-QST06 §B backpath (+3 quests, task_kind betray, an ending reached by breaking the intended path, >=1 irreversible act the game warns about but permits) and RI-EXP05 LH12/LH16.
note: The three backpath quests carry act: null so that the act census in tools/quests/mainline-census.mjs counts 5/5/5/8/5 and reports these separately, which is what they are. The word backpath appears in every one of their notes for RI-QST06's own jq. Q-MAIN-32 is the aftermath and is also act: null.

quests.title: The Cut

giver.location: Blackrose, the cutting yard behind the reed-walk
giver.disposition_min_note: W1-19 round 2 re-clamp. Round 1 set every clamped gate to the WORST signature's COLD-START standing at this giver, measured by an offer-gate probe that only ever looks at frame zero. That left all nine clamped gates with a worst-case margin of exactly 0, and the piece's own first quest then moved the derived faction term by -12, so eleven of forty signatures could not finish and the main quest closed itself twenty-two quests later. This number is set from `tools/quests/mainline-chain-floor.mjs`, which measures the standing at this giver at EVERY STEP of both chains for all forty signatures, with consequences accumulating and no topic hand-fed. The rule: a gate keeps its rank order and its race discrimination, and sits far enough below the measured chain floor that the shortfall left is one a purse can close (RI-DLG04 §C, seam S15). Availability is never a function of birth; price is.

quests.directions: The eleven live roots that feed the intakes come up under the Deep Marshes between Sunken Barrow and the edge of the Stone Wastes, in standing water, and the nearest of them is a morning out of Sunken Barrow along the causeway that is under water at the top of the tide. The skei does the work. Nobody has given leave for any of it and nobody is going to.

journal.text: There is a way at this that does not need the Court, the chapter, the writ, the barges or the eight voices. Eleven live roots in standing water between Sunken Barrow and the Wastes, a cutter's knife, and about nine days. Neeja-Xul will not come and has told me how.

The first root took four hours and it is the smallest of the eleven. What comes out of a live root when it is opened without leave is not sap, at first. I am not going to describe it here. The intake below it stopped within the day and I felt the change through the water.

The well at Sunken Barrow went cold on the third day and the well at Mudwater Landing on the fifth. I knew this would happen. I proved it would happen with my own hand on the sixth intake and a man is buried for it. I am doing it anyway and I want that written down in the order it happened.

Six of eleven and the interior has worked out what is doing it. There are keepers standing at the seventh root. They are not armed and they are not going to move and there is no way to open that root that does not go through where they are standing. I am the thing they are standing there about.
I stopped at the seventh root. Six intakes shut, four wells cold on the coast, no route down, and the keepers are still standing there. Whatever I have done to this province I have done half of it.

Eleven roots in nineteen days. The keepers at the seventh moved, in the end, because Neeja-Xul came out and stood between us and talked to them for a night, and she has not spoken to me since. The intakes are shut and the way down through the root channels is open and there are nine wells cold between here and Soulrest.

Eleven roots, and I went round the seventh instead of through it, which took six more days and a route under the barrow that is not a route. None was moved and none was hurt and the wells went cold exactly the same, which is the part that has stayed with me.

branches.condition: The player goes through the keepers at the seventh root, or six days round under the barrow, or stops

resolutions.outcome: All eleven roots are cut in nineteen days. Nine wells go cold between the Deep Marshes and Soulrest, the intakes are shut, and the root channels are open as a way down that goes under everything the Court holds.
The same eleven roots, six days longer, without going through anybody. The wells go cold identically, which is the point of offering the route.

failure_states.cause: The player stops at the seventh root
failure_states.consequence: Six intakes shut, four wells cold, no route down. The damage stands and the backpath is not open; the intended route through Act IV is still available and considerably harder, because four of the eight voices now know what the player has been doing in the Deep Marshes.

deceit.stated_objective: Cut eleven live roots and shut the intakes from below
deceit.actual_objective: Cut eleven live roots and shut the intakes from below
deceit.truth: Shutting the intakes shuts the wells above them, which the player proved by hand in Q-MAIN-12 and which this quest states plainly at journal index 30 before the third root is touched. The game warns and permits.

rewards.name: the root channels under the Wastes
what nine cold wells look like
what Neeja-Xul said to them that night
the route under the barrow that is not a route

quests.notes: Backpath quest 1 of 3. RI-QST06: a route that reaches an ending by breaking the intended path, requiring at least one irreversible act the game warns about but permits. The warning is journal index 30, in the player's own voice, before the damage is done; there is no modal, no confirmation and no UI string anywhere in it.

quests.title: The Severed Thread

giver.location: Soulrest, the Drowned Court's archive under the burial stair

prerequisite_topics: the ninth clause of the Drowned Tally

quests.directions: The archive under the burial stair at Soulrest, through the door that is always wedged. Hosk-Vei is still there. He is always there. Whatever has happened above him, he has thirty years of the same room and he will hear you out in it, which by this point in the business is not nothing.

journal.text: A person the Recension needed is dead and I am the reason. The clause cannot be read the way the Court reads it any more and the sextons have stopped calling me the tally-reader. Hosk-Vei sent for me. He did not send for me to shout.

He says the Court has been here before. Three times in four hundred years the claimant has been wrong or the claimant has broken it, and each time the Court wrote it down and carried on, because the book is longer than any of them. He read me the three entries. They are all in the same dry hand as everything else.

The mandate is void and the machine is still running. Nothing about the second sentence depends on the first. Whatever I am, and I am now certainly not what the chapter room said I was, there is a reservoir under the Stone Wastes filling up and a man in it keeping a ledger, and I know the way down.

Hosk-Vei will write me a fourth entry. Not a mandate, not a claim, not a clause. A line in the Tally saying that in the ninth sap-fall a person who was owed nothing went down without the Court's leave and what came of it, and he says he will write it either way and that it will be read in a hundred years by a reader like me.

I did not go back to the archive. The word tally-reader is not said in front of me in Soulrest any more and the crypt road is shut and I have no idea what to do next, and the sound under the Wastes has not changed at all.

The thread is cut and it does not matter. The Court will write me a line in the Tally either way and the machine does not care what any book says about me. Whatever is left of this I do without a mandate, which is roughly what Bel Mourne has been saying since the beginning.

I asked Hosk-Vei to write the fourth entry before I went down instead of after, so that it says what I intended and not what happened, and he refused, and then he did it, and it is the only page in that archive that was written by a hand that did not know how it came out.

branches.condition: The player asks the archivist to write the entry before the descent rather than after

resolutions.outcome: The mandate is void, the player carries on without one, and the Tally records the severance in the same dry hand as the other three. The route down is whatever the player has already opened.

The archivist writes the fourth entry before the descent, stating the player's intention rather than the outcome. It is the only page in the archive written by somebody who did not know how it came out, and it is quoted back at the player in the aftermath.

failure_states.cause: The player never returns to the archive after the severance
failure_states.consequence: No fourth entry and no route stated. The backpath is still reachable through Q-MAIN-29 and the aftermath has one fewer thing to quote at the player.

deceit.stated_objective: Find out what the Court does about a claimant who has broken the claim
deceit.actual_objective: Find out what the Court does about a claimant who has broken the claim
deceit.truth: It has happened three times in four hundred years and the book carried on each time. Whether the claim was ever genuine is exactly as unsettled after the severance as before it, and the severance is not evidence either way.

rewards.name: the book is longer than any of them
the fourth entry, written before the descent

quests.notes: Backpath quest 2 of 3, and seam S10's implementation for the mainline. RI-EXP05 LH16: an ending is reachable after killing a quest-critical NPC and the game says so in the player's own journal voice rather than in a modal. Opened by the world state rather than by a giver's offer — the topic is seeded from hooks.json when mandate_void is raised by QuestEngine.npcDied.

quests.title: The Drowned Count

giver.location: Sunken Barrow, the head of the root channels

quests.directions: The root channels start at the seventh root under Sunken Barrow and go in under the Wastes below everything the Court holds. They are full of water for most of their length and empty where the intakes have stopped. Nobody has walked them. Nobody has been able to before, because before the cut they were live.

journal.text: The channels go in under the Wastes below the crypt road, below the gallery, below the ash. They are empty now because I emptied them. It is four days in the dark with the walls going soft where the roots were and there is no camp, no writ, no barges and not a soul behind me.

I came up into the working parts from underneath, which has not been done, and the keepers on the counting floor did not know I was there for a day and a half. Two of the bays are dead already, from the roots I cut, and the people who kept them are sitting in them.

Ixtu-Meer knew. He has known since the third root. He has been sitting in the counting chamber for nineteen days with a ledger going wrong in front of him and no way to stop it and no interest in leaving, and when I came up out of the floor he asked whether I had come the long way and whether I wanted to sit down.

The conversation is the same conversation. He makes the same case, which is still good, and this time I have already done half of what he is arguing against and he knows it and he makes it anyway. The reservoir is bleeding through six shut intakes into channels I opened and it will empty on its own in about a season whatever either of us does.

I did not get through the channels. Two days in, the roof came down where a root had been holding it, and I came back out of Sunken Barrow with nothing. The channels are not passable now and I am the reason for that too.

I opened the last sluices from below and the Count went down into the channels I had cut for it rather than into the roots, which is not what opening it was supposed to mean. Four thousand years of pattern went past the trees entirely and into the dark. The wells will not come back. Ixtu-Meer watched the whole of it from the stair and said one thing at the end, which was that this was also a way.

I shut the channels behind me with the last of the skei's edge and made the reservoir bleed into the roots after all, over a season instead of in an afternoon, badly, with six intakes dead and the allowance drifting. It is the worst version of the right answer and it is the one I could reach from where I had put myself.

I killed him in the counting chamber with the channels open below us and the reservoir going down past the trees, and it made no difference to anything at all, which I think I already knew when I did it.

branches.condition: The player lets the Count drain through the cut channels past the roots, closes the channels and forces it into the roots over a season, or kills the Steward with the channels open

resolutions.outcome: The reservoir empties into the cut channels and past the trees into the Void. The tide does not resume. The wells do not come back at all, anywhere, permanently, and the province persists.

The channels are shut with the last of the skei's edge and the reservoir bleeds into the roots over a season instead of an afternoon, with six intakes dead. The tide half-resumes. Everything works worse and nothing is finished.
The Steward is killed while the reservoir is already draining past the roots. It changes nothing that was going to happen and the journal says so.

failure_states.cause: The channels are entered before the eleventh root is cut
failure_states.consequence: The root channels are impassable for good. The backpath is closed and the mainline can then only be finished through the Court's gallery, which requires the Act IV voices the cut has already cost.

deceit.stated_objective: Reach the Count from below without the Court
deceit.actual_objective: Reach the Count from below without the Court
deceit.truth: He knew from the third root and did not leave. The reservoir empties in about a season whatever anybody does, and what is being decided on the backpath is only where it goes, and one of the two answers is past the trees.

rewards.name: the province afterwards, on the backpath
the skei, with no edge left
it made no difference to anything at all

quests.notes: Backpath quest 3 of 3. This is the ending reached by breaking the intended path: no chapter vote, no writ, no barges, no eight voices, no sill, and a world state that differs from the intended ending in more than thirty flags. RI-EXP05 LH12 and the RI-QST06 requirement that the ending world flag reached by this route differs from the intended one. The giver record names Neeja-Xul because the route is hers, but there is no disposition_min on it: the quest is discovery "consequence" and is opened by the world, and by this point in the backpath she is not speaking to the player, which is the point.

quests.title: The Season After

giver.location: The Bone Ladder, the sapwell under the rib

quests.directions: Everywhere. The wells that are still wells are where they always were and the ones that are not are also where they always were. Teeja-Lun is at the Bone Ladder if she is anywhere. The province is a fortnight across on foot and there is nothing stopping anyone walking it.

journal.text: It is done and I am still here and it is the eleventh of Sun's Height. There is no ceremony and I have not been sent for. The Bone Ladder well is doing whatever it is now going to do and Teeja-Lun is sitting beside it finding out, the same as everyone else.

The things people say to me now are all different and none of them are about prophecy. A carter asked whether the coast road is safe. A sexton asked what I want done with the ninth chair. Ojal-Weeth asked whether Sesh-Weth's name should go in the book as a burial or as something else and I did not have an answer for her either.

There are eleven things in this journal I never finished. The two of Weeja-Sen's people who were never accounted for. Whoever told the Blackwood Company. Why the eleventh root opened itself in the night. Why the tree at Thorn asked for me. They are not going to be closed and the province has gone back to being a place with weather.

I have walked from Soulrest to Stormhold and back to see what changed, which took eighteen days, and the honest answer is that most of it did not. What changed is at the wells and in eleven specific rooms, and everywhere else the reeds are doing what reeds do. I can walk the province asking, or I can kneel at the Ladder and find out on my own skin, and the first answer I get is the one I will believe, so it matters which I do first. Walking it first closes the other, because whichever answer I get first is the one that stands.

There is no season after, for me. I took the ledger and the ledger is worked from down here and I have not been up the eleven steps since. Ei-Vashan sends word down twice a year with whoever is coming anyway. She says the reeds are doing what reeds do.

I have been to nine wells and four settlements and asked people what they think happened. No two agree. Two of them think it was another's doing. One of them thinks nothing happened and that the Court made all of it up, and I could not prove otherwise to him in an afternoon and I did try.

Teeja-Lun asked me to sit at her well and I did, and whatever it does now it did to me, and it is different and it is not nothing. She asked whether I would have done it again and I said yes and she said that she asked because she wanted to know whether I would say it quickly.

branches.condition: The player walks the province afterwards, or sits down at the Bone Ladder well and finds out what it does to them now

resolutions.outcome: The player walks the province after the ending and hears nine different accounts of what they did, none of which agree and one of which denies it happened. Everything unfinished is still there and still doable.
The player kneels at the Bone Ladder well after the ending and finds out first-hand what the wells do now, which depends entirely on which ending was reached and is different in all five.

failure_states.cause: The player took the Steward's place and does not leave the reservoir floor
failure_states.consequence: There is no aftermath to walk. The player is the thing at the bottom of the shaft and the province is above them, and the refusal is delivered in the player's own journal voice rather than by a menu.

deceit.stated_objective: Find out what the province is like now
deceit.actual_objective: Find out what the province is like now
deceit.truth: Nine accounts, none of which agree, one of which denies it happened. The game does not supply a correct one.

rewards.name: the man who thinks nothing happened
whether I would do it again

quests.notes: The aftermath, and it is not a backpath quest despite living in this file; act: null because it is outside the five acts. RI-EXP05 LH13: the world is playable afterwards, with observable changes, and the one ending that has no aftermath — taking the Steward's place — refuses it in fiction through fail_never_came_up rather than through a menu. LH14: there are no credits, no score, no completion percentage and no grade anywhere in this file or in the engine.
